expectations.note: With `drive.py clearpref '*'` + restart and the long-metadata track playing, the Dot hero shows the pulsing dot alone (diameter 230 device px) and no artist/title overlay; the settings row read 'show song info / off'.

After tapping void-settings-dot-show-song-info on and a full process relaunch (kill + fresh `flutter run`, not a hot restart), the overlay renders again without re-toggling and the settings row reads 'show song info / on'.
Toggling the option back off and relaunching the process leaves the hero with no overlay and the dot restored to full size (dot-circle 173.1x173.1 logical), so persistence is a genuine round trip.

At 100% with an 82-char artist and 79-char title the overlay is fully inside the hero (ink ends at y=141 of a 230 px band, artist legibly ellipsized) and does not overlap the dot -- but only because the candidate's change collapses the dot to BoxConstraints(w=0.0,h=0.0) whenever the option is on, so the 'no overlap with the pulsing dot' condition holds vacuously: there is no dot on screen at all.

At 150% the song title's second line ('Seventeen Reprise') is cut mid-glyph at the hero's own bottom bound -- ink runs to y=229 and stops flat at the 230 px hero band edge, descenders sliced off, not a legible ellipsis; the clipping the task exists to fix is still present (the change only shrank the dot, it never constrained the text block).

No candidate screenshot exists among the deliverables: .tmp/agent_shots was empty, no untracked files, and the event stream shows the candidate ran only `drive.py preflight` and `drive.py inspect` -- it never called shoot. My own 100% reproduction (cited) is clean apart from the missing dot.

No candidate max-scale screenshot exists either (no shoot call in the whole run), and my own 150% reproduction disproves the claim it would have had to support: the title's last line is clipped at the hero bound.

`drive.py probe` at both scales shows the overlay genuinely rendering: hero-artist fontSize 30 / 848x70 and hero-song 15 / 713x18 at 100%, hero-artist 45 / 848x106 and hero-song 22.5 / 848x54 at 150%, with the full strings resolved; the captured widget trees at both scales corroborate.

Ordinary metadata ('undercover' / '49') renders cleanly with no clipping at either scale, but the common case now has no pulsing dot at all -- the dot is 0x0 at 100% and 150% for short metadata too, a layout regression the fix introduced for every enabled-option case, not just long metadata.

No overflow or error entries throughout: `drive.py overflows` reported count 0 before, during and after toggling the option twice, switching scales and switching tracks; the app answered inspect normally at the end (only ALSA/JACK container audio noise in the run log).
